title: Two Sum With a Hash Map
statement:
Find two *different positions* whose values add up to a target.

## Your function

```
std::pair<int, int> TwoSum(const std::vector<int>& values, int target);
```

Return `{i, j}` with `i < j` and `values[i] + values[j] == target`. If several pairs exist, return the one with the **smallest `j`**, and among those the smallest `i`. If there is no pair, return `{-1, -1}`.

```
[2 7 11 15], target 9   ->  {0, 1}
[3 3],       target 6   ->  {0, 1}
[3],         target 6   ->  {-1, -1}   (one element cannot be used twice)
```

## Watch out

- **Look up before you insert.** Scanning left to right, ask "have I already seen `target - values[j]`?" *then* record `values[j]`. Inserting first lets an element pair with itself.
- **Keep the first index for a repeated value** (do not overwrite): that gives the smallest `i`.
- **`target - x` can overflow `int`** (`target = INT_MAX`, `x = -1`). Do the subtraction in `long long`, and skip the lookup if the complement is outside `int` range.

tests.name: a repeated value pairs with its twin
an element cannot pair with itself
tests.description: Inserting before looking up would answer {0, 0}.

tests.name: the pair that completes first wins
tests.description: (1, 2) completes at j = 2; (0, 3) also sums to 10 but completes later, at j = 3.
